subject: Hybrid commit + overage protections proposal for BrightLight
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen@brightlight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hybrid commit + overage protections proposal for BrightLight

Hi Helen —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a short proposal that tries to balance BrightLight's desire for predictable unit economics with Redwood's need to plan capacity. High-level idea: a small monthly commit (reserved tokens) + usage-based overage priced below hosted list, with explicit rate-protection guardrails. Key points in the attached term sheet: 

- Commit tier: $40k/mo committed usage (applies to token-equivalent consumption).
- Overages: billed per-token at $0.00055 (vs public list $0.00075) for the next 12 months.
- Price lock: base per-token prices for committed and overage tiers locked for initial 12-month term; after that annual adjustment with CPI cap.
- CPI cap: annual increase tied to US CPI, capped at 3% (we proposed 3%).
- MFN: mutual most-favored pricing limited to hosted API published tiers and peer customers in same region; carve-outs for negotiated enterprise promos.
- Overage protections: 60-day notice before any non-contract price changes; automatic fallback to a compatible quantized-variant model if capacity constrained.

I've attached the term sheet and a simple worksheet with math showing how different consumption patterns map to effective unit price. Please review and let me know which parts are deal-breakers for your procurement team.

If helpful, I can produce a 1-pager showing 12-, 18-, and 24-month TCO scenarios under three usage curves.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-hybrid-term-sheet-v3.pdf (term sheet, 3 pages); pricing-examples-brightlight.xlsx (consumption scenarios)
From: Helen Park <helen@brightlight.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightlight.ai
Date: 2026-10-04T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid commit + overage protections proposal for BrightLight

Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the worksheet. A few clarifying Qs from procurement and finance: 

1) CPI cap — we need clarity on the indexing and lookback. Is Redwood using the US CPI-U (all items) with a 12-month lookback? Is the 3% cap absolute or is it a cap on the applied CPI?
2) MFN — procurement is worried about an overly broad MFN that would allow retroactive price parity for any promotional pricing Redwood publishes. We need MFN scoped to equivalent committed-hosted offers with the same or higher annual commitment and similar term.
3) Price lock window — would you consider a 6- or 12-month price lock on overage rates after an announced change? Public customers will expect some runway.

Also: can you provide an example where BrightLight grows 2.5x in a quarter — how would overages and the commit interplay? The worksheet was helpful but a quick example embedded in the term sheet would speed approvals.

Looping in procurement; they may follow up with redlines.

Best,
Helen Park
Head of Product Operations, BrightLight
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen@brightlight.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-06T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid commit + overage protections proposal for BrightLight

Helen —

Thanks, great questions. Quick answers and a suggested compromise we think is fair to both sides: 

1) CPI indexing: we use US CPI-U (all items), 12-month lookback, applied on the anniversary of the effective date. The 3% figure is a hard cap on the increase we can apply in any given year. If CPI is negative, we pass through downward adjustments.

2) MFN scope: agree we should narrow. Proposed wording: MFN applies only to public hosted API price tiers for committed offers with equal-or-greater annual committed spend and identical billing model (monthly/monthly-in-advance vs annual). Promotions targeted at a partner program or channel (e.g., marketplace listing promos) are excluded. We can add an exceptions schedule to the SOW.

3) Price lock window: we're proposing a 12-month initial lock for both commit and overage base rates. After that, CPI-U adjustments (capped) apply annually. On top of that we can offer a 60-day advance notice for any non-contractual published list price changes that could affect future renewals.

Example (requested): assume monthly baseline committed 40k USD and BrightLight runs a burst quarter at 2.5x average consumption (effective monthly consumption during the quarter = $100k equivalent). Overages billed at $0.00055 will apply to tokens above the committed bucket for that month. Because the commit is monthly, BrightLight's committed capacity will cover $40k of that $100k for the month; the remaining $60k billed at the overage rate. Over the quarter we'll auto-apply a rolling commit reconciliation (statement-of-usage) so you only pay for actual usage; if you sustain higher levels we can discuss an uplift to committed tier mid-term with retro credits for the month the uplift takes effect. I attached an updated worksheet with this scenario highlighted (same file name).

If procurement wants a guaranteed per-year CPI cap of 2% instead of 3% to satisfy finance, we can evaluate that as a concession in exchange for a 24-month firm term and a minimum annualized commit. Thoughts? Marissa, tagging you for pricing approval if we move CPI cap down to 2% in exchange for term/commit.

-Karthik

Date: 2026-10-08T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Hybrid commit + overage protections proposal for BrightLight

Karthik / Sean —

I reviewed the ask. We can move on the CPI cap but need clear trade-offs. Approve the following delegate: 

- CPI cap reduced to 2% (from 3%) only if BrightLight signs a 24-month firm term and commits to $480k annualized minimum (equivalent to $40k/mo).
- Maintain MFN scope as you proposed (committed-hosted offers only, exclusions for partner promos).
- Offer a 90-day price-lock on overage rates at renewal (instead of 12 months post-contract) — this protects Redwood operationally while giving the customer runway.

If Helen accepts the 24-month firm term + $480k annual, we can finalize with legal and include a short carve-out allowing Redwood to offer time-limited promotional credits (explicitly excluded from MFN).

Please draft the small amendment to the term sheet reflecting these exact trade-offs and I will sign-off. 

Marissa
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
